description_medium: The Justice Department lists Stephen Bannon among the pardons Trump granted on January 19, 2021. Its entry identifies a Southern District of New York case involving conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to commit money laundering, and records no sentence.
description_long: The Justice Department’s pardon list places Stephen Bannon in its January 19, 2021 group and identifies his case as one in the Southern District of New York. The entry therefore documents the pardon and the offenses associated with the case, but it does not provide a narrative of the alleged conduct, the procedural posture, or the warrant’s scope. title: Pardons William E. Henry
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to William E. Henry as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department lists William E. Henry among the pardons granted on January 19, 2021. It identifies a Middle District of Alabama theft-of-government-property case and records two years’ probation and a $4,000 fine, imposed in 2019.
description_long: William E. Henry appears in the Justice Department’s January 19, 2021 pardon list. The entry identifies his case as one in the Middle District of Alabama and names theft of government property as the offense. It records two years of probation and a $4,000 fine, imposed on May 2, 2019. It also does not state why the president chose this case or reproduce the terms of the pardon. The recorded sentence supplies useful case context, but it is not a substitute for the underlying judgment or clemency warrant. title: Commutes Sentence of Theodore E. Suhl
description_short: Trump commuted the sentence of Theodore E. Suhl as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s July 29, 2019 commutations list names Theodore E. Suhl, convicted in the Eastern District of Arkansas. It records an 84-month prison term, three years of supervised release, and a $200,000 fine for honest-services wire fraud, federal-program bribery, and Travel Act offenses.
description_long: The Justice Department’s commutations list places Theodore E. Suhl in the July 29, 2019 group. It identifies his case as one in the Eastern District of Arkansas and records an original sentence of 84 months in prison, three years of supervised release, and a $200,000 fine. The listed offenses include aiding and abetting honest-services wire fraud, bribery concerning programs receiving federal funds, and Travel Act violations. These details show the seriousness and federal-program context of the case before clemency. The DOJ table does not describe the transactions involved, identify the public program or officials, or give a reason for the commutation. It also does not state how Suhl’s sentence changed under the grant. The entry can document the commutation and original judgment, but the resulting sentence and the conduct behind the offenses require the warrant or case record.
notes: The DOJ commutations list confirms Suhl’s district, original sentence, offenses, and July 29, 2019 group. It does not state the commutation’s new sentence or explain the underlying transactions or rationale.

title: Commutes Sentence of Jaime A. Davidson
description_short: Trump commuted the sentence of Jaime A. Davidson as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s commutations list records Jaime A. Davidson in its January 19, 2021 group. His Northern District of New York case resulted in life plus five years in prison and five years of supervised release for cocaine offenses and the murder of a DEA agent in furtherance of a drug conspiracy.
description_long: Jaime A. Davidson appears in the Justice Department’s January 19, 2021 commutations list. The entry places his case in the Northern District of New York and records a sentence of life imprisonment plus five years, followed by five years of supervised release. The listed offenses include conspiracy to distribute cocaine, four distribution counts, murder of a DEA agent, murder of an agent in furtherance of a drug conspiracy, and use of a firearm during drug trafficking. These are the original judgment details recorded by DOJ; the list does not narrate the events, identify the agent, or explain Davidson’s individual conduct. It also does not state the sentence imposed after commutation. Because the original and reduced terms are materially different facts, the clemency warrant or a case-specific account is needed to describe what Trump changed and the consequences of the grant.
notes: The DOJ commutations list provides the original life-plus-five-year sentence and offense labels but not the underlying events, Davidson’s role, the new sentence, or a documented reason for clemency.
